title: Cohomological dimension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$. All sheaves below are sheaves of abelian groups. On either site, put $F[\ell^r]=\ker(\ell^r:F\to F)$ for $r\geq0$, and call $F$ *$\ell$-power torsion* if the canonical map $\varinjlim_{r\geq0}F[\ell^r]\to F$ is an isomorphism, with the inclusions as transition maps. This is the local torsion convention; no common exponent is required. Take the following suprema over $q\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ in $\mathbf Z_{\geq0}\cup\{+\infty\}$, whose empty supremum is $0$.

For a qcqs scheme $S$ and a qcqs morphism $g\colon X\to Y$, the
*$\ell$-cohomological dimensions* are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)&=\sup\{q: H^q(S_{\Proet},F)\neq0
  \text{ for some classical $\ell$-power torsion sheaf $F$}\},\\
\operatorname{cd}_\ell(g)&=\sup\{q: R^qg_*F\neq0
  \text{ for some classical $\ell$-power torsion sheaf $F$ on }X_{\Proet}\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

For a field $K$ we write $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(\Spec K)$.

By the cohomology comparison and the direct-image comparison these are the usual
$\ell$-cohomological dimensions computed on the étale sites, so the classical
bounds apply. If $K$ is a field with $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)<\infty$, then
$\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)$ and $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(g)$ are finite for all
schemes $S$ and morphisms $g$ of finite type over $K$ (Stacks Project, Tag
0F10).

Here the small pro-étale site is [sk-def-pe-site], classical means [sk-def-pe-classical-definition], and qcqs and finite type have the conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The notation $H^q(S_{\Proet},F)$ means $\mathcal H^q(R\Gamma(S_{\Proet},F))$, where $\Gamma$ is evaluation at the terminal object $S$; $R^qg_*F$ means $\mathcal H^q(Rg_*F)$, where $(g_*F)(V)=F(V\times_YX)$ is the direct image on the small pro-étale sites [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image]. Both right derived functors are as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], applied to a sheaf in degree zero. The étale notation in the comparison clause is that of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. In the last sentence $g:X\to Y$ is a $K$-morphism between finite-type $K$-schemes, in the sense of [def-weil-scheme-over-base].

proof.text: The annihilator diagram laws follow from the kernel universal property. Factor ell^s as ell^(s-r) times ell^r to show annihilation; cancel the target kernel inclusion for identity and composition. Naturality is kernel.lift_iota. For an abelian sheaf on either site, the canonical annihilator cocone is a colimit iff sections are locally annihilated by powers of ell: a sheaf colimit is sheafification of the presheaf colimit, whose sections locally have stage representatives. Conversely AB5 makes the canonical map mono, and local annihilation gives explicit sectionwise kernel lifts, making it epi. This also gives ordinary torsion since prime powers are positive. All these arguments are proved in private Lean helpers, using the Mathlib abelian-group colimit and sheafification APIs.

source.place: opening local torsion convention and annihilator diagram

proof.text: Use the set-valued classical-image/counit criterion [det-pe-classical-sheaves-image]. The canonical forgetful pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-pullback-forget-comparison] respects units. Applying the adjunction hom-equivalence and triangle identities proves that it respects counits. Forgetting abelian group structure reflects isomorphisms, so an abelian pro-etale sheaf is classical iff its abelian comparison counit is invertible. The exact fully faithful comparison inverse image preserves and reflects the annihilator colimit: kernel comparison isomorphisms identify the diagrams and their cocones; preservation and reflection of colimits identify their colimit properties. Isomorphism invariance is proved with the local criterion. This directly treats abelian sheaves, without converting them to integer-module sheaves.

source.place: comparison sentence: coefficient objects and torsion

proof.text: For an etale abelian sheaf in degree zero, apply the generic existing source-library comparison adjunction. Its underived unit is invertible [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-grothendieck-unit], and comparison inverse image sends injectives to comparison-direct-image-acyclic sheaves [lem-pe-comparison-injective-left-modules-acyclic]. The existing generic criterion [lem-cbc-derived-unit-injective-acyclicity], Adjunction.isIso_derivedPlus_unit_app_of_rightAcyclic, makes the bounded-below derived unit invertible. Compose this with the bounded-below/unbounded compatibility and comparisonLowerStarCompRightDerivedGlobalSectionsIso [lem-weil-pbc-derived-sections-pushforward] to identify etale and pro-etale derived sections. Taking degree n homology and the coefficient identification in the previous step equates the sets of degrees in the two suprema. This is the abelian-coefficient proof of the cohomology comparison clause, using the existing generic API instead of the larger module-coefficient boundedBelowComparison statement.

source.place: cohomology comparison sentence; Stacks Tags 099V and 099W

proof.text: Use nonempty_iso_comparisonUpperStar_comp_rightDerivedLowerStar from WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.Comparison, the existing generic Grothendieck-abelian version of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. Take degree n homology, use exact inverse image commuting with homology, and bounded-below/unbounded and single-functor compatibility. The result is an isomorphism from nu_Y^* R^n g_et,* F to R^n g_proet,* nu_X^* F. It is used only inside a proposition: no arbitrary isomorphism is chosen as definition data. Additivity preserves zero and faithfulness reflects zero by testing identities. The coefficient identification then equates the two relative degree sets and their suprema. The qcqs assumptions are exactly those of the generic comparison theorem; the extra coherence assertions of the module-coefficient wrapper are not needed.

Finite type over a field makes the source locally Noetherian by Mathlib, giving the needed quasi-separatedness instances. The relative part of [lem-kun-0f10], in convention [def-kun-cd], gives an infimum of natural torsion-vanishing bounds strictly below infinity. sInf_lt_iff supplies an actual bound e. Every ell-power torsion sheaf is ordinary torsion by the local criterion above. The relative comparison turns a degree above e in the defining supremum into a nonzero etale higher image, contradicting this bound. Transport the vanishing through rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility; sSup_le proves dimension at most e, hence finite. The original field-dimension hypothesis is retained although unused for this relative result.

source.place: last sentence: relative finiteness; Stacks Tag 0F10

proof.text: Prove the abelian-sheaf stalkwise ell-power torsion criterion. Forward: stalks preserve the annihilator colimit, and an element has a stage representative, annihilated by ell^n. Backward: AB5 makes the colimit map mono. To prove epi, test two maps after every kernel inclusion on conservative geometric stalks; exactness lifts each stalk element annihilated by ell^n into that kernel. Thus the maps agree and the colimit map is invertible. This uses [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] and Mathlib filtered-colimit representatives. Apply [lem-sbc-qcqs-higher-images-prime-torsion] with the singleton {ell}. A positive integer with no prime divisor except ell is ell to the length of its prime factor list, including 1=ell^0 (Mathlib Nat.eq_prime_pow_of_unique_prime_dvd). Transport between the degreewise and total bounded-below right-derived conventions. The stalk criterion then shows that every higher direct image is ell-power torsion.

source.place: last sentence: fixed-prime torsion preservation; Stacks Tags 0DDC and 0DDD

proof.text: Use the absolute comparison to turn the finite field dimension into a natural etale bound c. A nonzero degree p>c would belong to its defining supremum and contradict that bound. Convert derived cohomology to Sheaf.H with [lem-weil-pbc-sheafH-ext-derived-comparison]. For the structure map s, the relative torsion bound from [lem-kun-0f10] supplies e. Every higher image is ell-power torsion by the preceding step, so its cohomology over the field vanishes above c. Apply [lem-sc-leray-vanishing-bound] to the actual higher-image functors to obtain vanishing on X above c+e. Convert back through the same Ext/derived isomorphism. Then sSup_le bounds the etale dimension by c+e; absolute comparison proves the pro-etale assertion. The argument includes zero sheaves, exponent zero, and empty schemes.

source.place: last sentence: absolute finiteness and Leray rectangle bound

proof_origin.place: T5: complete Lean proofs of all nine original holes. Kernel-colimit local torsion, abelian classical counit transport, generic source-library cohomology and higher-image comparisons, relative torsion bounds, stalkwise fixed-prime preservation, and the Leray bound; Stacks Tags 099V, 099W, 09A6, 0F10, 0DDC and 0DDD.
